Series::besselj¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

Series Series::besselj() const
Series Series::besselj(double order) const

Oscillatory Cylindrical Solutions¶

besselj() evaluates the Bessel function of the first kind, J_order(x), elementwise. It is the solution of

x² y'' + x y' + (x² - order²) y = 0

that is finite at the origin for non-negative order. It appears when a wave, diffusion process, or eigenproblem is expressed in cylindrical coordinates. Use the no-argument form for order zero; it is exactly besselj(0.0). Pass an order when the radial mode or analytic formula requires another member of the family. The order is one scalar shared by every lane; it does not broadcast from another Series.

Integer orders are evaluated without perturbing the order, including the parity relation J_n(-x) = (-1)^n J_n(x). Non-integer orders use the real power-series branch for non-negative x. A negative argument with non-integer order has no generally real value and returns NaN. order itself must be finite.

The operation is out of place and preserves shape and platform. It returns a real floating Series; integral input promotes to float64. No reduction or broadcasting occurs.

Reverse Mode¶

The local derivative uses the neighboring-order recurrence

d J_v(x) / dx = (J_(v-1)(x) - J_(v+1)(x)) / 2

For order zero this simplifies to -J_1(x). An incoming sensitivity is multiplied lane-wise by that value.

Examples¶

Example 1. The omitted order evaluates J_0.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0}).besselj());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.9385, 0.7652, 0.2239, -0.3971]

The sign change by x=4 is normal: J_0 oscillates and crosses zero.

Example 2. Order one selects a different radial mode.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0}).besselj(1.0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.2423, 0.4401, 0.5767, -0.0660]

Example 3. Fractional order is accepted on the non-negative real branch.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0}).besselj(0.5));

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.5410, 0.6714, 0.5130, -0.3019]

Example 4. Reverse mode for J_0 produces -J_1.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.besselj().sum().reverse();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.2423, -0.4401, -0.5767]

Example 5. A non-finite order is rejected before lane evaluation.

try {
  (void)pluss::make_series({1.0}).besselj(
      std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity());
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  const std::string message = e.what();
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

bessel: order must be finite
